## Recovered outcome, scope and verification

## Outcome

OpenHax is the responsive, fun head of a Knoxx deployment. Independent makers keep creating original music, lyrics, MIDI and visual work. Bluesky is the preferred publication outlet, with occasional Discord sharing. Operator conversation must never interrupt a maker.

## Scope

This planning change records the operator intent, recovered source links and an epic with five UUID-linked story slices: reserved head admission (3 provisional points), real creative cycles (5), event/publication (3), owner/job recovery (proposed 8) and lifecycle/cloud placement (proposed 5). It includes a read-only diagnostic and an operational evidence report for existing-capability repairs. It does not implement or qualify the proposed isolation, publication or recovery laws. Cards are authored incoming Markdown; Rheos has not admitted or transitioned them.

The recovered local consumer is active: native lyrics, original SVG/PNG artwork, and a verified12-second musical project have been delivered. As of20:10:50UTC, four natural15-minute clock cycles had completed across an intentional idle backend recreation and contract reloads: original SVG/PNG artwork, real music/lyrics and another image. The fourth saved a numeric16-second spec, lyrics, a matching16.000-second WAV and receipt, and delivered an independently verified audio attachment to Discord; its Bluesky post is a text announcement. Clipping metrics and optional tool failures remain recorded. This proves the clock resumed, not in-flight job recovery or uninterrupted cadence. A correctly specified native child maker also completed independently while the head acknowledged its actual run ID; an acknowledge-first follow-up exposed batched tools and a default-contract fallback rather than the requested maker. The head story now requires native acknowledgment ordering and strict delegated-shape validation. The evidence report distinguishes the served image, contract snapshot, directHTTP probe and actual Discord reply, and records the shared FIFO, soft publication guidance, native music parser bug, image provider403 and unverified sleep availability. Operational experiments continue independently, with exact evidence and limits, while this source plan is reviewed. The old cloud consumer stays disabled so the same identity has one gateway owner.

## Planning walkthrough

- Independent head story AC1–3 and AC7 requires a held-maker test and lane-local FIFO; increasing a shared queue's concurrency alone is not the promised guarantee. AC7 includes a batched send/spawn response and rejects silent child-contract fallback.
- Creative-cycle AC3 distinguishes dispatch admission from full job completion, addressing the existing schedule lock's short lifetime.
- Publication AC3–4 requires reconciliation/dedup and runtime frequency limits; prompt advice alone cannot prove these laws.
- Lifecycle/cloud-placement AC1–3 makes cloud availability explicit: the current local host does not establish availability during sleep, and Docker network reachability does not establish a mesh scheduler.

See `docs/verification/cephalon-always-on-20261006.md` for native artifact/run identities and limits.
